candidate.derivation: matrix-free lhs/u match dense-oracle Ndx/u elementwise to <1e-9 relative on a 96-param first system; bit-identity of the split rebuild vs solvePhase7b7DenseSystem holds on all 56 studied systems.
formulas: t = A·dx (packed CSR, no dense A)
z = P·t with packed upper entries applied exactly once per orientation (diag once; off-diag both)
y = P·w; u = A^T·y; r = lhs - u
signal relRes = ||r|| / max(1, ||u||); study tolerance 1e-9 (production PHASE7B6_CORRECTION_TOLERANCE untouched)
candidate.valueFaultRangeRelative: 5.6e-13 (dx-bias-1e-12, S3-accepted) .. 1.15 (sign flip); S3-rejected value faults start at 5.6e-9 (dx-bias-1e-8)

A better (scaled) estimator is future work, not a 10Q item under NO-GO.

floorEstimates.target10to15ms: The candidate's own cost (0.24ms) meets <=10-15ms trivially, but cost is not the gate — safety is. No strategy reaches the target WITH S3-equivalent acceptance except S3 itself.

gate: GATE D — no substitute: keep S3, stop the candidate line. Residual verification is ~230x cheaper (0.24ms vs ~58ms at 384) but has PROVEN unexplained false accepts on weak geometry (2/56 systems) that no metadata/condition composition repairs without reintroducing S3-equivalent cost or rejecting 85% of valid solves. No 10Q shadow proof (GATE A requires ZERO unexplained false accepts). No further certification (GATE B) because the failure is structural (near-null N directions), not a calibration gap. No condition optimization (GATE C) because the estimator is 100x above threshold on valid solves while passing the rejected case. S3 stays authoritative and untouched; candidate modules remain test-only and unreachable by production.
independenceVerdict: The candidate reuses the SAME assembly inputs (packed design/weights/misclosures) as the system under test, so assembly/packing corruption is invisible to it (shared-blindness, §22). Against ALGORITHM faults (wrong dx, damping, stale pairing, wrong system) it agrees with S3 except along near-null N directions, where only S3's direct correction comparison sees the error. Reusing the native factorization for verification would collapse the remaining algorithm independence — rejected without prototyping. S3's dense rebuild (independent accumulation + independent scaled/damped Cholesky) remains the only independent check.

s3Purposes.D-normal-consistency: dense rebuild itself (unpack + P + N + solve)
s3Purposes.E-conditioning: finite condition + threshold-excess WARN-ONLY + first-system/result.condition agreement within 1e-9

s3SplitNote: True S3 cost excludes the study's bit-identity double-rebuild (~13-16ms at 384, measurement overhead only). Dominant: redundant dense factorization (59%) — the same N the native backend already factored; reusing it would destroy verification independence (§22). Dense-P build (20%) + accumulation (16%) are the matrix-materialization price of independence.
staleProofs: 22/22 stale/wrong-system pairings reject under BOTH S3 and candidate (13 prev-iter + 9 same-dims-diff-network; includes same-N diff-RHS acceptance-difference behavior). Staleness is not the candidate's failure mode; weak geometry is.

tenQRecommendation: None (GATE D stops the line). If weak-geometry verification is ever revisited, the prerequisite is a scaled condition estimator that sits below threshold on the 13/14 valid cases here while flagging the dist-heavy mechanism — a new study, not a continuation.
toleranceSeparation: NO global separation: minFault (3.4e-16, metadata-only faults) < maxValid (2.6e-13). Restricted to VALUE faults on well-conditioned systems, the window (2.6e-13, 5.6e-9) separates at 1e-9 — but weak-direction faults (3.7e-10) fall inside it, so the window is unsafe. No tolerance change proposed or made.
